title: AI-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy
summary: In the journal abstract, an AI-ECG model trained on more than 330,000 ECG–echocardiogram pairs detected the dilated-cardiomyopathy phenotype (AUROC 0.87–0.97) and predicted later disease (C-index 0.80–0.87). In familial cohorts, five-year negative predictive values were 95.5% in Antwerp and 91.5% in Maastricht; positive predictive values were 42.4% and 39.4%. These are diagnostic and risk-prediction findings, not demonstrated clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Explainable deep learning model applied to electrocardiography
organization: Imperial College London; University of Antwerp and Antwerp University Hospital; Maastricht University Medical Center; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University

evidence.tested: Validated in UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital and Antwerp cohorts, and in two familial cohorts (Antwerp n=166, Maastricht n=177), compared with traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype from ECG; explainable AI-ECG outperformed traditional ECG parameters.
